statement: Phase 0.3 locking reads use one deterministic fail-fast reservation-conflict policy with machine/prose semantic agreement: participant owns acquire/conflict and emits typed contention; DistributedTransactionCoordinator owns the follow-on whole-transaction conflict abort, confirms rollback/release of earlier reservations before terminal transaction_aborted, owns timeout/cancellation/commit/rollback/recovery, no waiter queue or local TTL exists, and the architecture document and machine-readable policy encode the same owner/action/outcome table.

constraints.statement: Supersedes sealed locking-read-wait-policy-seal after PR #91 found missing conflict-abort ownership and a policy/prose consistency gap. Preserve the original seal unchanged.
Partition transaction participant alone owns reservation acquire/conflict and returns typed locking_read_reservation_conflict without waiting.

DistributedTransactionCoordinator alone owns the follow-on conflict abort: rollback whole transaction, confirm participant reservation release, then emit terminal transaction_aborted with contention cause.
No waiter queue, wake owner or hold-and-wait state exists; deadlock is impossible by construction in the initial slice.
Participants never independently expire unresolved reservations; release authority is transaction resolution.
The machine-readable policy and architecture prose/table must agree on owners, actions, outcomes, fail-fast/no-wait, deadlock, TTL, PG-wire ownership and future supersession.
